messages:
anya: Noticed an odd p99 jump for /v1/generate after we shifted routing weights this morning. p50/p95 look fine but p99 up ~200ms. anyone on call?
monitoring-bot: ALERT: endpoint=/v1/generate p99 above expected (baseline 340ms -> 550ms) at 08:12 UTC
sam: saw the alert. timeline matches the route-weight change at 07:58. could be a tiny sub-population causing the tail.
luis: important: are these percentiles computed at the gateway or downstream worker? provenance matters.
mike: gateway-side percentiles. I pulled histogram slices by origin tag, looks like route-3 spiked. quick dump: ```
# p99 by origin (pre vs post)
route-3: 340ms -> 680ms
route-1: 320ms -> 335ms
route-2: 360ms -> 370ms
```
anya: route-3 moved more traffic to dedicated-pool-3 which uses different batch tuning (higher batch_wait). could explain long tail for small fraction of requests.
sam: batch_wait change? who rolled that?
jen: that was in release/2026-03-21 for the dedicated pools. batch_wait_ms: 2 -> 7 on pool-3 to improve throughput.
luis: increasing batch_wait can add variance for single-request flows; you'll see skew only in upper quantiles if most requests still hit fast path.
mike: also seeing kv_cache_hit=false tagged requests concentrated on route-3. p99 for cache-miss is ~1.1s. volume is small (~0.6% of traffic) but enough to skew p99.
anya: so twin causes: batch_wait higher + cold KV caches on the new pool. fix options: prewarm top prefixes, lower batch_wait for that pool, or change routing weights back.
sam: can we surface kv_cache breakdown in the console quickly? right now need to write a custom query.
jen: created a quick metrics tag: `kv_debug=true` on the pool for 1hr so we can split dashboards.
mike: ran query: `increase(inference_latency_bucket{endpoint="/v1/generate",kv_cache_hit="false"}[10m])` shows ~50 cache-miss events in 10m, p99 ~1.05s.
luis: small absolute count but big p99 effect. console suggestion: let percentiles be annotated with sample_count and top contributing tags (hover). would avoid chasing false positives.
anya: agree. filed console ticket CONS-412: "percentile provenance + sample count hover". cc @jen for prioritization.
sam: short-term action: roll back batch_wait on pool-3 to 2ms and kick prewarm for top 200 prefixes. long-term: enforce a routing-change checklist.
jen: prewarm command: `./tools/prewarm --pool=pool-3 --keys-file=top-prefixes.txt --concurrency=8` started at 08:35 UTC.
mike: rollback applied 08:40 UTC. metrics warming up; initial p99 dropping to ~420ms at 08:46.
luis: suggest also an alert refinement: if p99 jump corresponds to sample_count < 0.5% of endpoint traffic, mark as "low-sample" and surface guidance rather than firing full-incident.
anya: I'll add a runbook item: before changing route weights, validate batch/cache parity and prewarm status. simple checklist PR incoming.
sam: after prewarm finishes, can we add an automated dashboard snapshot that shows p50/p95/p99 split by kv_cache_hit and origin for the last 15m? helps verification.
mike: yes. creating a temporary dashboard panel now.
monitoring-bot: NOTE: created incident INC-2026-058 (p99 spike /v1/generate) - link: internal/INC-2026-058
jen: prewarm finished 08:48 UTC. post-prewarm p99 for route-3 now ~430ms. overall endpoint p99 ~430ms at 08:50.
anya: nice. follow-ups: 1) runbook checklist PR (anya) 2) console provenance hover (CONS-412) 3) alert tweak for low-sample p99 noise (sam) 4) dashboard panel snapshot automation (mike). assign and ETA in the ticket.
luis: one more idea: compute a "stable-quantile" by downweighting buckets with sample_count < threshold to prevent noisy p99 flips in UI. might be controversial but worth prototyping.
sam: noted. might be better as an annotation + educational tooltip rather than changing the raw percentile.
anya: agreed. ok team — next check in 1h, will close thread if stable. thanks. :white_check_mark:
